newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile rains may be heavier than normal - forecast.
newsitem.headline: Chile rains may be heavier than normal - forecast.

text.p: Chile's national weather service on Thursday said heavier-than-usual rains could fall during the next three months as the result of the so-called El Nino phenomenon in the Pacific Ocean.
"During the next three months, there is a 60 percent probability of a period of normal or slightly heavier rainfall compared with the usual climate," the service said in a statement.
Although El Nino is still in an early stage, it is already having an effect in warming the surface of the ocean off Ecuador, Peru and northern Chile, it said.
Chile has suffered a severe drought in recent months, which has depleted reservoirs, the country's largest source of electricity.
In April, the government imposed emergency measures, including a five percent cut in power voltage, to save electricity.
